reasoning: First admissible round, 0% map, no priors. Anchor on the Okuda route (parent 2: growth + reaction-diffusion patterning + monolayer mechanics) and knock out one operator at a time so each effect is attributable against a single control. Test the target-mechanism coupling (add shape_energy_3d:default), the necessity of patterning (remove cell_diffuse), and the necessity of topological remodeling (remove reconnect_t1_3d). These three establish the load-bearing levers before any combination map is worth building.

slots.claim: the parent, unchanged -- the Okuda growth-driven monolayer route with RD patterning
layering the default shape-energy coupling onto the growth-driven monolayer amplifies emergent protrusions above control
slots.why: This edit yields the 'target mechanism' region; Okuda states coupling patterning to deformation is what produces tubulation/branching, so the coupled shape energy should raise protr_peak over the monolayer baseline. REFUTED if the extra shape energy over-stiffens and protr_peak falls below control.

slots.claim: removing morphogen diffusion abolishes the reaction-diffusion pattern that localizes deformation, collapsing protrusion height
slots.why: Okuda's thesis is that PATTERNING must be coupled to deformation; without diffusion the RD prepattern cannot form, so if patterning is truly load-bearing protr_peak drops toward the unpatterned floor. Adversarial because growth+mechanics may still buckle the sheet on its own, which would refute the necessity of RD.

slots.claim: without T1 topological transitions the sheet cannot remodel neighbors, so it cannot resolve into discrete tubes
slots.why: Okuda always includes T1 remodeling; suppressing it is outside his published space and isolates whether topological neighbor exchange is necessary for tube individuation rather than mere bulging. Excursion because a no-remodeling regime is never shown -- it should reveal whether tube COUNT is set by topology or by growth alone.
